### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s).

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5ecf9374701d3fcb9de439c0bc09f7008992c80a`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5ecf9374701d3fcb9de439c0bc09f7008992c80a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7241a6f1bbac601810e54aee8065e2be1e9a4534` — the merge of head `d726cc761765087c4ba038ed8690c4872255a845` into base `5ecf9374701d3fcb9de439c0bc09f7008992c80a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7241a6f1bbac601810e54aee8065e2be1e9a4534 && git checkout 7241a6f1bbac601810e54aee8065e2be1e9a4534
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5ecf9374701d3fcb9de439c0bc09f7008992c80a d726cc761765087c4ba038ed8690c4872255a845 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5ecf9374701d3fcb9de439c0bc09f7008992c80a && git merge --no-ff d726cc761765087c4ba038ed8690c4872255a845

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5ecf9374701d3fcb9de439c0bc09f7008992c80a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5ecf9374701d3fcb9de439c0bc09f7008992c80a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cxk4f4T7at3YeFruhZ

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `d726cc761765087c4ba038ed8690c4872255a845` (announced in 7030195390).

**Gates on this head:** 53 check-runs: 37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both passed. Mergeable: clean.

**What I checked (holds):**
- **Arm A as ruled (7023449707), riders 7023599246 met:**
  - `declinable` is opt-in. Without it, `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` (~1562) still throws the refusal, so `aggregate_records` and its three callers keep the 400, untouched.
  - The "Refused, never approximated" docblock is amended. The engine itself still never sorts or cuts in process: a decline reads nothing and answers `[]`.
  - Select and lookup label-ordered keys never reach the cut. The dataset executor orders those in memory and hands this face no window (`canPushDownWindow`). This is pinned: "a lookup dimension ordered by its display label is never cut in the database".
- **The decline has its own slot.** `declined` is separate from `outcome`, so `AggregateOrderCutOutcome` (`kind: 'served'`) keeps its type. `AggregateOrderCutDecline` stays off the package root (`d726cc76`). A request built wrong (an order key naming no column) is still refused either way, and that is pinned.
- **The seam mirrors `executeRelationGroupAggregate`.** It uses the same engine (`requireDataEngine`) and the same `engineAggregateQuery(input)`, so `context` (the ADR-0021 D-C principal), `filter` with `withReadScope` and `timezone` all travel exactly as in `executeAggregate`. No read-scope belt is lost. The request rides a `Symbol.for` read option, so no wire request can carry it. `served` is trusted only when `outcome.kind === 'served'` and `totalGroups` is a number; anything else falls back to memory.
- **The strategy's cut is the in-memory cut's membership:**
  - `limit` is `offset + limit`, and `windowServedCut` then applies `applyWindow(rows, limit, offset)`, which skips only the offset.
  - Measure keys use the measure's full name, which is the alias the aggregate input sets. Dimension keys use `resolveFieldName`, the same short column the remap reads.
  - Any order key naming neither a measure nor a projected dimension makes the face skip the cut, so it never reaches the engine's INVALID_SORT.
  - `totalGroups` comes from the statement through `groupCountRequestOf`, and the in-memory path still uses `answerWholeGrid`.
  - No row filter sits between the aggregate and the window. The remap and the best-effort `sql` echo are the only steps.
  - The cross-object path (`executeCrossObject`) is untouched.
- **Tests.** The face pins cover:
  - measure top-2 with `totalGroups`;
  - offset;
  - text collation with NULL last both ways;
  - the `/analytics/query` door;
  - a reference-zone decline;
  - the lookup-label pin;
  - memory-driver fallback;
  - Turso-local / WASM served.

  The objectql pins cover decline per non-compiling driver, `having` and in-memory bucket declines, compiling-driver parity, and the wrong-built refusal. The ablation in the body fails exactly the 4 database-cut pins and leaves the 3 fallback pins green, which is the right split.
- **Changeset.** One patch entry each for `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/service-analytics`. It states the visible text-order change and the decline list (memory, MongoDB, OData, Turso remote, uncompiled bucket or zone, unevaluated measure filter). `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are correct. `Fixes #35287` is right: arm A is delivered, and the card's narrower win is what the riders already recorded.

**On the seat's question (is `declinable` a contract face):** in my reading it is not a new one. It is an optional field on the exported TS type `AggregateOrderCutRequest`, plus an engine-written `declined` slot. It is reachable only in process through a `Symbol.for` read option, and absent it nothing changes. That is additive and not authorable, and it is not on the wire. The contract-visible change in this PR is the text top-N order on compiling drivers, and the maintainer's arm A ruling already decided it. A separate contract read is your call, but L1 sees nothing in this PR that the ruling does not cover.

**Notes (non-blocking):**
1. As the dev notes, the dataset executor re-sorts the N served rows with its in-memory comparator. Membership is the database's, but the order within the top-N can differ from the database collation on text ties and case. The native face does the same today.
2. A `limit` with no `order` is now cut by the group keys ascending (the engine's full order) on compiling drivers. Before, it took the first N in arrival order. This is deterministic now and was arbitrary before; the changeset could say so in one clause.

Not governed (no `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**` or spec), so the area lands it.
